nodes.title: A third candidate doubles the tokens for no endpoint
nodes.claim: 2 candidates -> 3 candidates on the same chain, planner and tree: tokens 14,486 -> 30,254 (2.09x), round clock 572,217 -> 827,189 ms (1.45x), graded endpoint mean -0.025 with interval [-0.074, 0.024] (cannot distinguish below 0.070). Decision reject:budget-mismatch, read off the ledger rather than off a test.

nodes.title: An arm that changes two things at once still has a decision, just not a cause
nodes.claim: ab-cand2b -> ab-cand4 read reject:budget-mismatch too, but it also restored the planner, so it cannot say which change cost the tokens; the clean pair is ab-cand1b -> ab-cand4 (same chain, same planner, only the candidate count differs). Both files are kept: the confounded pair still answers 'is this configuration worth running', the clean pair answers 'is the third candidate worth buying'. Naming which question a comparison answers is cheaper than avoiding confounded comparisons, which the schedule does not always allow.
